events.text: You gave a jade hairpin to the newest member of the household. Nobody told you that {npc} has been asking for one for six years. At dinner {npc} smiles at everyone, eats very little, and thanks you for the soup with a politeness that could cut silk.

choices.text: Buy {npc} a finer one at once (20 taels)

mem.note: bought me a hairpin to stop a quarrel

effects.log: {npc} accepts the pin and does not wear it. A pin bought to end a quarrel is a receipt, not a gift.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to walk with you after dinner

effects.log: Under the plum trees {npc} says nothing for a long time. Then: "Six years." You did not know. Now you do.

choices.text: Pretend you noticed nothing

effects.log: The soup gets saltier every night that week. Someone in the kitchen has taken a side.

events.text: The hairpin has gone missing. The newest member of the household is in tears. Two servants say they saw {npc} near that room. {npc} says, very calmly, that {he} has no need of other people's trinkets, and goes back to the household accounts without looking up.

choices.text: Search the house yourself, quietly

ok.log: The pin is in the magpie's nest on the roof, with a spoon and two buttons. Everyone laughs, a little too loudly.

fail.log: You find nothing, and {npc} knows you searched {his} rooms with the rest. The quiet grows.

choices.text: Defend {npc} before the household

effects.log: You say it plainly: {npc} does not steal. The servants look at their feet. {npc} looks at you.

choices.text: Ask {npc} straight out

mem.note: asked if I was a thief

effects.log: {npc} puts down the brush. "After all these years, you ask me that." The door closes softly.

events.text: {npc} comes to you at night with two cups of tea and sits down without being asked. "I was the first," {he} says. "I kept this house when it was one room and a leaking roof. I do not want to be loved most. I want to be remembered."

choices.text: Give {npc} the household seal, before everyone

mem.note: gave me the seal of the house

effects.log: The next morning the seal hangs at {npc}'s belt. Nobody in the house mistakes the meaning.

choices.text: Tell {npc} about the leaking roof years

effects.log: You remember the bucket, the cold rice, the one blanket. {npc} laughs and cries at once and the tea goes cold.

choices.text: Say every spouse is equal here

mem.note: said I was only one of many

effects.log: It is fair, and it is the wrong thing to say tonight. {npc} nods, and takes the cups away.

events.text: {npc} has stopped coming to the evening meal. Nobody noticed for three days, which is the whole problem. You find {him} in the back courtyard, mending a robe that does not need mending. "In a loud house," {he} says, "the quiet ones turn into furniture."

choices.text: Spend the whole of tomorrow with {him}

effects.log: One day: the market, the river, a bad noodle stall. {npc} talks more in that day than in the last year.

choices.text: Give {him} a room and a task of {his} own

mem.note: gave me a place of my own

effects.log: {npc} takes over the herb garden and turns it into the best in the district. People ask for {him} by name.

choices.text: Tell the household to be kinder

effects.log: Everyone is very kind to {npc} for a week, which is worse. Then they forget again.

events.text: It begins with a seat at the ancestral rites. The children of two of your spouses both expect to stand nearest the tablets. {npc} has already had a new robe made for {his} child, in the colour only an heir wears. The other side of the house has noticed.

choices.text: Name no heir yet. Rites by age only

effects.log: Eldest first, at every rite. It is fair. Nobody in the house thinks it is fair.

choices.text: Have the robe dyed another colour

effects.log: The robe comes back a sad brown. {npc} hangs it where you will see it every day.

choices.text: Set a test of merit for all the children

effects.log: A test in letters and in arms, in three years. The whole house goes very quiet and starts studying.

events.text: The household has split into two courtyards, and the servants into two parties. Somebody has written to the clan elders. Somebody else has hired a tutor from the capital at a ruinous price. {npc} tells you, calmly, that if you do not decide, the house will decide for you.

choices.text: Call all the spouses together and decide

ok.log: A long night. Shouting, then tears, then terms. By dawn the house has one heir and one peace.

fail.log: The night ends with a broken screen and no heir. You sleep in the study. (-4 health)

choices.text: Send the eldest children to a sect to grow up

effects.log: With the children on a mountain, the quarrel has nothing to stand on. It sulks, and shrinks.

choices.text: Let the elders of the clan choose

mem.note: gave my child to the elders' judgement

effects.log: The elders choose the child whose parent sent them the best ginseng. Everyone knows it.

events.text: Years later, the two rival children are old enough to have opinions of their own. They meet you in the hall together, which they have not done since the quarrel began. They have talked it out between themselves, they say, without any of their parents. {npc} stands at the back of the hall, unsure whether to be proud.

choices.text: Hear their terms and accept them

effects.log: One keeps the house; the other keeps the sword school. They shake hands like merchants. You feel very old.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the children did better than us

effects.log: {npc} laughs, really laughs, for the first time in years. "They did. Gods help us, they did."

choices.text: Overrule them. The choice is yours

effects.log: They bow and obey. Neither of them asks your advice about anything again.

events.text: A guest of rank is coming to dinner, and the household must be seated. Who sits at your right hand? Three people have three different opinions, and each opinion arrives with a story about a promise you made years ago, which you do not remember making.

choices.text: Seat everyone by the date of marriage

effects.log: Old custom, no arguments. The guest compliments the order of your house. The quiet is mostly real.

choices.text: Seat yourself alone at a small table

effects.log: The guest finds it eccentric and charming. Your spouses find it so absurd they forget to quarrel.

choices.text: Let them draw lots for it

effects.log: The lot falls to the one who started it. Nobody believes the lots were fair. Somebody checks the bowl.

events.text: Your cook will not cook for one courtyard, your gatekeeper delivers letters to the other courtyard last, and the laundry comes back mixed up on purpose. The servants have joined the quarrel in your household, and they are much better at it than the spouses.

choices.text: Dismiss the worst two as a warning

effects.log: Two servants go. The rest become remarkably neutral. The cook stays, and sulks in butter.

choices.text: Raise everyone's wages (25 taels)

effects.log: Money buys a fragile peace in the servants' hall, and gossip about you instead of the spouses. (-25 taels)

choices.text: Have the spouses cook together for a day

effects.log: Burned rice, cut fingers, one magnificent stew. The servants watch in horror. The spouses laugh. (-3 health)

events.text: A teacup breaks against a pillar in the inner courtyard. Nobody saw who threw it. Everybody heard it. When you arrive, {npc} is sweeping up the pieces alone and will not say whose hand it was, only that it was not about the tea.

choices.text: Help {him} sweep, and ask nothing

effects.log: You sweep together in silence. At the end {npc} says, "Thank you." It is about more than the sweeping.

choices.text: Demand to know who threw it

ok.log: The thrower confesses, ashamed, and apologises to the pillar and the house. The air clears a little.

fail.log: Nobody confesses. Everybody is now a suspect. Dinner is a tribunal for a month.

choices.text: Buy a dozen new cups and say nothing

effects.log: Twelve new cups. Within a year, eleven. Still, eleven is more than one. (-6 taels)

events.text: Nobody in your household is speaking to anybody. Messages go by servant, by note, and once by a very confused child carrying a message in each hand. You are not sure what started it. You suspect it may have been you.

choices.text: Apologise to everyone, for everything

effects.log: A broad apology, nothing specific. It works, because everyone assumes it was for what upset them.

choices.text: Leave on a long training retreat

effects.log: You come back stronger. The quarrel has ended without you, and someone else got the credit.

choices.text: Break it with a terrible joke at dinner

ok.log: A groan, a snort, then helpless laughter round the table. Nobody remembers who was angry at whom.

fail.log: The joke dies on the table. The silence closes over it and gets one day longer.

events.text: An old woman of the district, famous for settling the quarrels of great houses, arrives uninvited with a basket of persimmons. She says your household's shouting can be heard at the well. She offers to mediate, for a fee, or for free if you let her keep the persimmon tree.

choices.text: Pay her fee (15 taels)

effects.log: She interviews everyone, alone, for an hour each. Her verdict is sharp, fair and humbling. It mostly holds. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Give her the persimmon tree

effects.log: She takes the tree, and the household's grievances, and somehow sorts all of them into baskets.

choices.text: Thank her, and send her away

effects.log: She leaves, and tells the well. By evening the whole district knows your household quarrels.

events.text: Famine in the next valley. Before you have finished reading the letter, {npc} has opened the granary ledger, one spouse is counting carts, another is writing to the rice merchants, and someone has already put on travelling clothes. They are waiting for you to say yes.

choices.text: Say yes, and go with the carts

effects.log: The household moves like a well-trained sect. Forty carts leave at dawn with your banner on the first.

choices.text: Say yes, and stay to guard the house

effects.log: You keep the house. They take the carts. It is strange, being the one who waits.

choices.text: Ask if the household can afford it

effects.log: {npc} shows you the sums, already done. It can. It just. You feel slightly unnecessary.

events.text: The relief carts reach the valley, and bandits reach the carts. Word comes back fast: your household drove them off with ladles, a borrowed spear, and one spouse's alarming skill with a carrying pole. Nobody is hurt. The valley calls your house the Ladle Army.

choices.text: Ride out to meet them on the road home

effects.log: You meet them at the ford. They are filthy and triumphant and want very much to tell the story at once.

choices.text: Teach them all proper staff forms after

effects.log: Every spouse turns up to train. Even {npc}, who complains about the hour every morning and never misses one.

choices.text: Embrace the name. Hang a ladle over the gate

effects.log: The ladle over the gate becomes famous. Beggars bow to it. Bandits avoid the road.

events.text: The valley sends a thank-you: a cart of first-harvest rice, a carved wooden plaque, and three orphans whose families did not survive the famine. The elders of the valley ask, very politely, whether your household has room. {npc} is already looking at you.

choices.text: Take the orphans in

effects.log: Three more at the table. The house is louder and poorer and better. Nobody regrets it.

choices.text: Find them good homes in the valley

effects.log: You pay for their keep with three good families. You visit, each spring, with sweets. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Hang the plaque and share out the rice

effects.log: The plaque reads The House of Ladles. You pretend to hate it. You keep it polished.

events.text: Lantern festival night. Your household has made one enormous lantern together, shaped like a carp, with each spouse responsible for one fin and nobody responsible for the tail. It is lopsided and magnificent. The neighbours are already laughing at it, fondly.

choices.text: Carry it to the river at the head of the house

effects.log: The lopsided carp floats down the river leading a thousand neat ones. Children cheer it all the way.

choices.text: Finish the tail yourself, badly

effects.log: Your tail is the worst part. Everyone says it is the best part. That is what a household is.

choices.text: Enter it in the district contest

ok.log: It wins Most Spirited, a prize invented on the spot by judges unable to stop laughing.

fail.log: It loses to a very correct crane. Your household cheers the crane. The crane's household is baffled.

events.text: An enemy of yours has been spreading poison about your house in the teahouses: that you are a fraud, that your spouses married for silver. {npc} has called a council in the inner courtyard. Every spouse is there. Nobody has called it a council of war, but there is a map.

choices.text: Let the household plan it

effects.log: The plan has seven parts and three of them are about tea. You are assigned part four. You do not argue.

choices.text: Say you will deal with it alone

effects.log: {npc} rolls up the map, and unrolls it again the moment you leave. You will be helped whether you like it or not.

choices.text: Ask what the enemy truly wants

effects.log: Silence round the table. Then the youngest spouse says: "Your seat at the Alliance banquet." Of course.

events.text: The plan unfolds. One spouse charms the teahouse owners. One finds the enemy's debts. {npc} writes letters to three great houses in a hand so elegant it is a threat on its own. Your part is to stand in the market and look unbothered, which is harder than it sounds.

choices.text: Stand there and look unbothered

ok.log: You stand in the market and buy persimmons for an hour. The town decides the rumours were silly.

fail.log: You glare at a fishmonger who did nothing wrong. The rumours gain a day. {npc} sighs.

choices.text: Challenge the enemy openly instead

ok.log: A short, clean duel in the square. The enemy yields. The household is proud and slightly annoyed.

fail.log: You lose, publicly. The household's plan has to cover for you too. It does. (-10 health)

choices.text: Help {npc} with the letters

effects.log: You are a worse writer than {npc}, who corrects your characters with visible pleasure.

events.text: The enemy comes to your gate in plain robes and asks to see the head of the house. You come out. So does the whole household, in a line, arms folded. The enemy looks at them, then at you, and bows lower than you have ever seen anyone bow.

choices.text: Accept the apology, and offer tea

effects.log: Tea on the veranda with a former enemy. The household watches every sip. It becomes a strange friendship.

choices.text: Let {npc} speak for the house

mem.note: let me speak for the house

effects.log: {npc} speaks for half a minute, very gently. The enemy leaves pale and polite, forever.

choices.text: Demand a public retraction

effects.log: The retraction is read at every teahouse. Your house's name is cleaner than before it was smeared.

events.text: You come home to find the whole household behind the door, holding their breath very badly. It is your birthday. They have been planning it for a month, they each had one job, and one of them has already told you by accident at breakfast.

choices.text: Act completely surprised

effects.log: You gasp. You are a terrible actor. Nobody cares. The cake is enormous and tastes of chestnut.

choices.text: Admit you knew, and thank them

effects.log: "Who told?" Everyone turns to look at the same person, who turns very red. The feast is wonderful.

choices.text: Insist they each get a gift too

effects.log: A birthday for the whole house. The servants want to know if they count. They do. (-10 taels)

events.text: Each spouse has planted something in the inner garden: one a plum, one herbs, one a row of cabbages for reasons nobody understands, one a single peony guarded like a treasure. The garden makes no sense as a whole. Guests always stop in it.

choices.text: Plant something of your own there

effects.log: You plant a pine. It will take forty years to look like anything. Someone ties a ribbon on it anyway.

choices.text: Sit there every morning to train

effects.log: The garden is good for breathing. The cabbages are oddly calming. You do not ask why.

choices.text: Hold a tea party in it for the district

effects.log: The district comes for the tea and stays for the cabbages. Your household is the talk of the season.

events.text: A fever lays you low for a month. You remember very little of it, only that there was always someone there. When you wake properly, you find a schedule pinned to the door in three hands: who sits with you, who boils the medicine, who reads aloud, who argues with the doctor.

choices.text: Keep the schedule, framed

effects.log: It hangs in your study. Visitors read it and go quiet. Some of them go home and make one.

choices.text: Cook for the whole house when you recover

effects.log: Your cooking is bad. Everyone eats all of it. It is the best meal the house has had all year. (+5 health)

choices.text: Ask what you said in the fever

effects.log: They exchange looks. "Nothing," they say together, far too quickly. You will never know.

events.text: Somebody brings out a zither, somebody a flute, somebody a drum nobody can play. The household's evening music is famous in the street: not good, but loud and very happy. Tonight the neighbours have brought their own instruments, which is either a tribute or a war.

choices.text: Play along, badly

effects.log: The street plays until midnight. The night watch stops to listen, and then to join in.

choices.text: Recite a poem to the music

effects.log: Your poem is better than the music. The music gets louder to compensate. It is a good night.

choices.text: Sit back and only listen

effects.log: You listen. The house you built is making music. Your qi is calmer than it has been in years.

events.text: Your spouses have established a household council, which meets each new moon and keeps minutes. You were not consulted. You have been invited to attend as a guest. The first item on the agenda is your habit of leaving swords on the dining table.

choices.text: Attend, and accept the ruling

effects.log: The motion passes four to one. Swords go on the rack. The minutes record your objection, beautifully.

choices.text: Propose an item of your own

ok.log: Your motion for a second bathhouse passes on the first reading. The council respects a good argument.

fail.log: Your motion is tabled indefinitely. You are learning what it is to be a junior member.

choices.text: Decline, with dignity

effects.log: The council meets without you. You discover later that they voted you a new robe. It is lovely.

events.text: A great house has offered you a match, and the offer is generous. Before you can reply, {npc} asks to see the letter. {He} reads it twice, folds it neatly, and says only: "If they come, they come through the front gate, and they bow to the house."

choices.text: Agree, and let {npc} set the terms

effects.log: {npc}'s terms are courteous, complete and impossible to misread. The great house accepts them all.

choices.text: Decline the match out of respect for {npc}

mem.note: turned down a great house for me

effects.log: The great house is offended. {npc} is quietly, enormously pleased, and pretends not to be.

choices.text: Tell {npc} it is not {his} decision

mem.note: said it was not my house

effects.log: {npc} bows, very correctly. In a few years you have never seen a bow that cold.

events.text: At the spring banquet, a visiting magistrate seats {npc} below one of your younger spouses, by mistake or by design. {npc} sits where {he} is put, with a pleasant face. Everyone at your table is looking at you to see what you will do.

choices.text: Rise and give {npc} your own seat

effects.log: You stand and offer your cushion. The magistrate goes pale. Every great house in the hall takes note.

choices.text: Correct the magistrate privately

effects.log: A word in the ear. The seats are changed between courses. {npc} squeezes your hand under the table.

choices.text: Leave it. It is only a banquet

effects.log: "Only a banquet," you say later. {npc} agrees. That is how you know you have done badly.

events.text: {npc} has been the keeper of your house for many years. Now {he} asks you for something of {his} own, which {he} has never done: a journey alone, a season away, to the place where {he} was born. The household will have to manage without {his} hand.

choices.text: Let {npc} go, with your blessing

mem.note: let me go home for a season

effects.log: {npc} goes. The house nearly falls apart. {He} comes back browner and younger and laughs at the accounts.

choices.text: Go with {npc}

mem.note: came with me to my village

effects.log: A village of thirty houses and one well. {npc} shows you every stone. It is the best season of your life.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to wait until next year

effects.log: {npc} agrees to wait. {He} has been waiting since the leaking roof. {He} is very good at it.

events.text: A new spouse has come into the house, young and nervous, carrying two boxes and an old sword. {npc} meets the newcomer at the gate with the household keys on {his} belt and a smile that tells you nothing at all. The whole house has found reasons to be in the front courtyard.

choices.text: Introduce the newcomer yourself, warmly

effects.log: You make the introductions. {npc} takes the newcomer's boxes personally. The house exhales.

choices.text: Leave the welcome to {npc}

effects.log: {npc} gives the newcomer the best room and a list of rules in perfect calligraphy. Kind, and very clear.

choices.text: Hold a feast to welcome them (20 taels)

effects.log: A feast. The newcomer is overwhelmed and drinks too little and smiles too much. It is a start.

events.text: The newcomer has made one mistake after another: the wrong door, the wrong ancestral tablet, the wrong cat fed. Last night they burned the rice for the whole house and wept in the kitchen. {npc} tells you about it. You cannot tell whether {he} is amused.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to take the newcomer under {his} wing

effects.log: {npc} teaches the newcomer the house, room by room. Within a year they are thick as thieves.

choices.text: Comfort the newcomer yourself

effects.log: You eat the burned rice with the newcomer, on the kitchen step. It is terrible. You both laugh.

choices.text: Tell the house mistakes are allowed here

effects.log: Everyone immediately confesses an old mistake. The cook's is the worst. The newcomer feels much better.

events.text: A rival house insults the newcomer at the market, loudly, about where they came from. Before you can move, {npc} has stepped between them, said three quiet sentences, and walked the newcomer home by the arm. The rival house sends an apology by nightfall.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what the three sentences were

effects.log: {npc} smiles. "Something about their grandfather's debts." You decide never to cross {him}.

choices.text: Thank {npc} before the whole household

effects.log: The household cheers. The newcomer cries again, for better reasons. The house is one house.

choices.text: Go and settle it with the rival house

ok.log: The rival house's champion yields in four moves. Nobody insults your household in that market again.

fail.log: You lose the bout and win nothing. {npc} bandages you and says it was already settled. (-8 health)

events.text: {npc} has kept the household keys for many years: granary, treasury, wine cellar, the little box nobody may open. Today {he} lays them in front of you. "I am tired," {he} says. "Choose who keeps them next, or keep them yourself."

choices.text: Ask {npc} to keep them a little longer

mem.note: asked me to stay the keeper

effects.log: {npc} takes the keys back with a sigh that is mostly relief. You hire {him} a steward for the dull parts.

choices.text: Give them to the next spouse in order

effects.log: The order is kept. {npc} teaches the next keeper for a year. The little box remains unopened.

choices.text: Keep them yourself

ok.log: You learn the granary, the treasury and the cellar. The little box you still do not open.

fail.log: Within a month the cellar is empty and the granary is full of mice. You return the keys. (-10 taels)

events.text: It is the anniversary of your wedding to {npc}, many years ago. {npc} remembers it exactly. You remember it as a blur of rain, a borrowed robe and a goose that would not stop honking. {npc} asks what you remember best.

choices.text: The goose

effects.log: {npc} laughs so hard {he} has to sit down. The goose, it turns out, is {his} favourite memory too.

choices.text: {npc}'s face, under the rain

effects.log: {npc} goes quiet and looks away. The rest of the day is very gentle.

choices.text: Take {npc} back to the place it happened

effects.log: The old hall is a teahouse now. You sit at the table where the altar was. Somebody's goose honks. (-8 taels)

events.text: {npc} has always wanted to open a shop: dumplings, or medicine, or brushes, the dream changes with the year. Today {he} shows you an empty storefront by the bridge and a list of costs written very small, so it will look like less.

choices.text: Pay for the shop (40 taels)

effects.log: The shop opens in spring. In a year it pays you back, with interest, and {npc} gloats. (-40 taels)

choices.text: Help {npc} build it with your own hands

effects.log: Two months of carpentry. The counter is crooked. {npc} says it is crooked because you made it, and keeps it.

choices.text: Say it is not the time

effects.log: {npc} folds the list away. The storefront by the bridge becomes somebody else's dumpling shop.

events.text: A letter comes for {npc} from the village where {he} grew up: the old teacher who taught {him} to read is dying and has asked for {him}. It is twenty days' travel. {npc} holds the letter and does not ask you for anything.

choices.text: Pack for both of you

mem.note: came with me to say goodbye

effects.log: You arrive in time. The old teacher holds {npc}'s hand and tells you three stories about {him} that {he} denies.

choices.text: Hire {npc} the fastest horses (20 taels)

effects.log: {npc} arrives in time and comes back a different, gentler person. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Send a gift in {his} place

effects.log: The gift arrives a week after the funeral. {npc} never mentions the teacher again. (-5 taels)

events.text: {npc} has been watching you train every morning for years. Today {he} picks up a practice sword and stands in the yard across from you. "Teach me," {he} says. "I am tired of only watching you go to fights."

choices.text: Teach {npc} properly, from the first stance

effects.log: {npc} is slow, stubborn and unexpectedly good. In a year {he} can disarm you, once, on a good day.

choices.text: Teach {him} only to defend

effects.log: Blocks and footwork, nothing more. {npc} grumbles. Then one night it saves {his} life on the road.

choices.text: Refuse. One fighter in the house is enough

effects.log: {npc} puts the sword down. Next month you hear {he} has found a teacher in town.

events.text: {npc}'s brother has run up a debt with a pawnbroker and fled. The pawnbroker now stands at your gate, very politely, with two large friends. {npc} is white with shame and has told you not to pay a single coin of it.

choices.text: Pay it, and say nothing more (30 taels)

effects.log: The pawnbroker leaves. {npc} does not thank you; {he} works it off over two years. You let {him}. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Respect {npc}'s wish, and refuse

effects.log: The pawnbroker goes to find the brother instead. The brother comes back much more polite.

choices.text: Show the pawnbroker's friends the door

ok.log: The large friends discover they have urgent business elsewhere. The debt is renegotiated downwards.

fail.log: The large friends were larger than they looked. The debt is renegotiated upwards. (-5 health)

events.text: Somebody from {npc}'s past turns up at the gate: a companion from the years before your marriage, ragged from the road and full of stories in which {npc} is much wilder than you have ever seen {him}. {npc} has turned a remarkable colour.
events.arc: An Old Friend at the Gate

choices.text: Invite the friend to stay a week

effects.log: A week of stories. You learn {npc} once stole a magistrate's horse. You look at {him} with new respect.

choices.text: Ask {npc} privately who this is

effects.log: {npc} tells you the whole story, which is better than the friend's version and much more embarrassing.

choices.text: Give the friend silver and send them on (10 taels)

effects.log: The friend goes, grateful. {npc} watches the road a long time after. (-10 taels)

events.text: You find a stack of pages hidden under {npc}'s winter robes: a novel, half written, about a martial artist with a terrible temper and a very patient spouse. You recognise yourself on the first page. It is not flattering. It is very well written.

choices.text: Read all of it, then ask for the ending

effects.log: {npc} is mortified, then delighted. The ending, when it comes, is kinder to you than you deserve.

choices.text: Put it back and say nothing ever

effects.log: Years later the book is published under another name. It sells everywhere. You buy six copies.

choices.text: Offer to pay a printer for it (25 taels)

effects.log: The book is a small sensation. Strangers look at you in the market and grin. (-25 taels)

events.text: Two of your children by different spouses have fought in the yard: a wooden sword, a split lip, a broken promise about a kite. Each parent has heard only their own child's version, and both versions are delivered to you at once, at volume.

choices.text: Hear the children, not the parents

effects.log: The children, asked alone, both tell the truth and both burst into tears. The kite is mended. The parents are not consulted.

choices.text: Punish both children equally

effects.log: Equal punishment, equal sulking. The two children are united at last, against you.

choices.text: Take both children to fly a new kite

effects.log: One kite, two children, one string. By the end of the afternoon they are a team. The parents are baffled.

events.text: Every spouse has an opinion about how the children should be taught. One wants poetry, one wants the sword, one wants accounts, one wants the children left alone to climb trees. The tutor you hired has fled, leaving a note that reads only: Too many parents.
events.arc: The Schoolroom of Many Mothers and Fathers

choices.text: Let each spouse teach one subject

effects.log: Poetry in the morning, the sword at noon, accounts after, trees at dusk. The children thrive in pure chaos.

choices.text: Hire a sterner tutor (15 taels)

effects.log: The new tutor ignores every parent equally. The children learn fast and complain constantly. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Side with the tree climbers

effects.log: A year of trees. The children grow strong and brown. Two of them become remarkable at lightness arts.

events.text: A new child, and the whole household wants to name it. There is a list. The list has twenty-three names on it. One of them is a joke. One of them is the name of a famous swordsman. One of them is, unaccountably, the name of the cook.

choices.text: Choose the swordsman's name

effects.log: A heavy name for a small person. The child grows into it, eventually, sword first.

choices.text: Choose the cook's name

effects.log: The cook weeps with joy. The meals improve beyond recognition. The child is very well fed.

choices.text: Let the eldest child choose

effects.log: The eldest picks a name that means "steady river". Nobody can argue. Nobody tries.

events.text: The inner palace has its own court, and its own wars. A minor consort's father is a minister you need. The minister has hinted that a promotion for the consort would be very warmly received. {npc}, your first spouse, has heard about the hint before you have.

choices.text: Ask {npc} for counsel first

effects.log: {npc} explains the minister, the consort, and the three other ministers who will be furious. It is a long night.

choices.text: Promote the consort. The minister matters

effects.log: The minister is delighted. The inner palace is not. The temperature drops by several degrees.

choices.text: Refuse. The palace is not a market

effects.log: The minister bows and goes very quiet in council. Quiet ministers are the dangerous kind.

events.text: A poisoned sweet is found in the inner palace kitchen, before anyone eats it. The eunuchs whisper that a certain consort's servants were seen near the ovens. {npc} has already sealed the kitchen and wants to know whether you want the truth, or a quiet answer.

choices.text: The truth, whoever it touches

ok.log: It was a cook paid by a minister's rival, not a consort. The consort is cleared, publicly. The cook is exiled.

fail.log: The trail goes cold in a ministry. Everyone in the palace now suspects everyone. Sleep is short.

choices.text: A quiet answer. Close it

effects.log: {npc} closes it. A cook is dismissed. You never learn whose hand it was, which may be wiser.

choices.text: Have the food tasted forever after

effects.log: Every dish is tasted twice. Your meals arrive cold for the rest of your reign. You are alive to complain.

events.text: The inner palace has settled into a careful peace, and {npc} has built most of it, one tea party at a time. Now the ministers want {npc} to formally hold the seal of the inner palace, which would make {him} a power at court in {his} own right.

choices.text: Grant the seal

effects.log: The seal ceremony is grand. From then on, ministers bring their quarrels to {npc} first. The court runs smoother.

choices.text: Keep the inner palace out of the court

effects.log: The walls stay high between the court and the inner palace. {npc} understands. {He} also keeps a list.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what {he} wants

effects.log: {npc} thinks about it for a day. "A garden, and no seal." You give {him} both gardens in the palace.

events.text: The old Grand Dowager of the previous reign still lives in the eastern palace, and still rules the inner palace from it. The Dowager has summoned {npc} to tea three times this month. {npc} comes back each time very calm, which you have learned is the worst sign.

choices.text: Visit the Grand Dowager yourself

effects.log: The Dowager receives you with great courtesy and tells you, kindly, that you are doing everything wrong.

choices.text: Let {npc} handle the Dowager

effects.log: {npc} goes to tea a fourth time, and a fifth. The calm becomes a little less calm. {He} is holding.

choices.text: Send the Dowager a costly gift (30 taels)

effects.log: The gift is accepted, admired, and placed in a storeroom with all the other gifts of all the other emperors. (-30 taels)

events.text: The Grand Dowager has made a move: a young relative of the Dowager's line is to enter the inner palace as a consort, with rank above {npc}'s. The court watches. Refusing a Dowager is not done. Accepting would put the Dowager's hand inside your house.

choices.text: Accept the relative, at a low rank

ok.log: The Dowager accepts the compromise with a dry smile. The relative turns out to be shy, decent and very bored.

fail.log: The Dowager takes it as an insult and says so, publicly. The court enjoys a delicious month.

choices.text: Refuse, with the grandest courtesy

effects.log: A refusal wrapped in six pages of compliments. The Dowager reads it all, and laughs, and lets it go.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to meet the relative first

effects.log: {npc} meets the relative and returns with a plan: the relative wants to be a scholar, not a consort.

events.text: The Grand Dowager is dying, and asks for {npc}, not for you. When {npc} comes out of the eastern palace hours later, {he} carries a small box and the old woman's last instruction: the inner palace is {his} to keep now, and you are to be told so.

choices.text: Bow to the Dowager's will

effects.log: The palace mourns the Dowager properly. {npc} keeps the box closed and the inner palace in perfect order.

choices.text: Ask what is in the box

effects.log: Fifty years of court secrets in a tiny hand. {npc} burns half of them. The other half {he} keeps.

choices.text: Hold the funeral rites yourself

effects.log: You lead the rites. The old ministers weep. The Dowager was hard, and held the palace for years.

events.text: A eunuch of the inner palace has been selling gossip to a minister: who visited whom, who wept, which consort you spoke to longest at the moon festival. The proof is in a ledger, and the ledger is now on your desk.

choices.text: Exile the eunuch quietly

effects.log: The eunuch goes to a temple in the far south. The minister learns nothing more. Neither of them is mentioned again.

choices.text: Feed the minister false gossip through him

effects.log: For a year the minister plans around a palace that does not exist. It is the best entertainment of your reign.

choices.text: Confront the minister in open court

effects.log: The minister falls on his knees before the whole court. The ministry is suddenly very interested in honesty.

events.text: The whole inner palace is out on the lake for the moon festival. Every consort's boat has been decorated to outshine the others. Lanterns, musicians, a boat shaped like a crane, a boat that is entirely peonies. They are all waiting to see which boat you step into.
events.arc: The Moon Festival in the Palace

choices.text: Step into {npc}'s boat

effects.log: Custom honoured. The lake applauds politely. {npc} hands you a cup of warm tea and a look of mild triumph.

choices.text: Row a small boat yourself, alone

effects.log: The emperor rowing a fishing boat badly between the great ones. Every consort laughs. Nobody is slighted.

choices.text: Have all the boats tied together

effects.log: One great raft of boats, all the consorts on it at once. The festival becomes a party. The cranes are offended.

events.text: The matchmaker has arranged a meeting at a teahouse, with a screen between the two of you, as old families still do. Through the screen {npc}'s voice is low and amused. "I am told you are tall, handsome, and kind to animals," {he} says. "Which of those is the lie?"

choices.text: "All three, probably."

mem.note: made me laugh behind the screen

effects.log: A laugh behind the screen, real and surprised. The matchmaker, listening at the door, writes something down.

choices.text: Ask what the matchmaker said of {him}

effects.log: "That I am rich, gentle and a great beauty," {npc} says. "I am one of those, on Thursdays."

choices.text: Move the screen aside

ok.log: {npc} looks at you a long moment, then pours tea. The matchmaker faints, briefly, from the scandal.

fail.log: {npc}'s chaperone gasps and puts the screen back. The teahouse will talk about it for a month.

events.text: The second meeting is without a screen, at a riverside pavilion, with three relatives of {npc}'s sitting at a nearby table pretending to look at the river. They are not looking at the river. One of them is taking notes.

choices.text: Go and greet the relatives first

effects.log: The relatives are taken aback, then charmed. The note-taker underlines something twice.

choices.text: Talk to {npc} as if they were not there

effects.log: You talk about books and swords and bad food. {npc} forgets the relatives too, for an hour.

choices.text: Suggest a walk somewhere they cannot follow

effects.log: Along the dyke, too narrow for three aunts abreast. {npc} laughs the whole way.

events.text: The matchmaker comes to collect your answer, with a face of professional serenity and a fee in mind. {npc}'s family has already sent theirs, sealed. The matchmaker refuses to tell you what it says until you give yours.

choices.text: Ask for time to know {npc} as a friend

effects.log: The matchmaker sighs. {npc}'s sealed letter, opened later, said exactly the same thing.

choices.text: Say yes, warmly, and mean it

effects.log: The sealed letter is opened: a yes, with a drawing of a teacup. Courtship may begin properly.

choices.text: Decline, kindly

effects.log: {npc}'s family is gracious. {npc} sends a short note: no hard feelings, and come to tea anyway.

events.text: Over tea, {npc} mentions the fine estate in the north that you own. You do not own an estate in the north. You own one sword and a goat. It emerges that the matchmaker told each of you a great many things, most of them extremely untrue.

choices.text: Confess the goat

effects.log: {npc} confesses in turn: no jade mine, no famous grandfather. You compare lies all afternoon.

choices.text: Go together to confront the matchmaker

effects.log: The matchmaker is unrepentant. "Did I lie about the important thing? You get on, don't you?"

choices.text: Maintain the estate story

ok.log: {npc} never asks to visit the estate. Some lies are allowed to die of old age.

fail.log: {npc} asks to visit the estate. You arrive at a goat. The goat is unimpressed. So is {npc}.

events.text: The matchmaker brings a portrait of a prospective match: a face of breathtaking beauty, the skin of a peach, eyes like autumn ponds. The matchmaker's nephew painted it. The matchmaker's nephew, you happen to know, has never painted anyone who looked like the painting.

choices.text: Ask to meet the person, not the portrait

effects.log: The person is ordinary-looking, witty, and laughs at the portrait harder than you do. A fine afternoon.

choices.text: Ask the nephew to paint you next

effects.log: Your portrait is magnificent and nothing like you. It goes out to six houses. Three reply.

choices.text: Decline the matchmaker entirely

effects.log: The matchmaker leaves with the portrait and a wounded professional air.

variants: The matchmaker unrolls a portrait: a face of impossible beauty, peach skin, eyes like autumn water. It was painted by the matchmaker's nephew, and you know for a fact that nobody he has ever painted looked like his paintings.
The matchmaker's new portrait shows a face like a spring morning. It is the nephew's work again, and the nephew, as half the town knows, has never once painted what was in front of him.

events.text: {npc} is the child of the family that has been feuding with yours for three generations. You met through a matchmaker who did not know, or who very much did. Both families are horrified. {npc} is not horrified at all. {He} keeps sending you excellent tea.
events.arc: A Match from the Enemy House

choices.text: Keep meeting {npc}, openly

effects.log: Every gossip in the district follows your walks. {npc} waves at them cheerfully.

choices.text: Meet only in secret

effects.log: A shrine at dawn, a library at dusk. The matchmaker keeps your secret for a fee you suspect is double.

choices.text: Send back the tea

effects.log: The tea returns. A week later, more tea arrives, with a note: "Try this one instead."

events.text: {npc}'s family has summoned you to their hall. The elders sit in a row. The family sword hangs on the wall behind them. {npc} stands at the side, pale and determined. The eldest elder asks why your house should be forgiven anything.
events.arc: A Match from the Enemy House

choices.text: Apologise for the old feud, sincerely

effects.log: A long silence. Then the eldest elder says, "Nobody has said that in sixty years." Tea is brought.

choices.text: Say the feud is not yours or {npc}'s

effects.log: The elders argue among themselves for an hour. You are not thrown out. That is something.

choices.text: Offer to duel their champion

ok.log: You win, and help the champion up. The elders grunt. A grunt, in this family, is very high praise.

fail.log: You lose, and keep standing up. The elders are impressed despite themselves. (-10 health)

events.text: Something has shifted between the two houses. Your family's elders and {npc}'s are seen drinking tea together in public, stiffly. The feud is not over, but it is tired. {npc} says it was the two of you that made it tired, and asks what you want now.
events.arc: A Match from the Enemy House

choices.text: Ask the two houses to sign a peace

effects.log: The peace is signed in the matchmaker's teahouse. The matchmaker charges both families a fee.

choices.text: Tell {npc} you want {him} as a friend for life

effects.log: {npc} laughs. "Only a friend? We shall see." The tea keeps arriving.

choices.text: Let the old houses sort themselves out

effects.log: The houses squabble, slowly forgetting why. You and {npc} take long walks and stay out of it.

events.text: Three matchmakers arrive at your door on the same morning, each with a portfolio, each certain the other two are frauds. They will not leave. They have begun arguing on your doorstep about whose candidates have the best teeth.

choices.text: Hear all three, one at a time

effects.log: Three hours of candidates. You remember none of them, except one who apparently raises ducks.

choices.text: Make them compete for your fee

effects.log: A bidding war in reverse. The winner offers to pay you to be their client. You accept.

choices.text: Flee over the back wall

effects.log: You spend the day at the river. When you come back, the three matchmakers have become friends and opened a partnership.

events.text: The matchmaker who introduced you to {npc} has presented a bill. It includes a fee for the introduction, a fee for the teahouse, a fee for the screen, and a fee described only as "emotional labour". {npc} has received an identical bill.

choices.text: Pay it, with good grace (15 taels)

effects.log: The matchmaker bows deeply and recommends you to everyone. Business is business. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Go with {npc} and haggle it down

effects.log: You and {npc} haggle as a team. The matchmaker is impressed. "You are well matched," they say. "I knew it."

choices.text: Refuse the emotional labour fee

effects.log: The matchmaker tells three teahouses you are cheap. The other fees are paid. Your reputation pays the rest.

events.text: {npc} has begun sending you poems. They arrive every three days, by servant, folded into the shape of a crane. They are not good poems. They are earnest, slightly too long, and they rhyme "sword" with "sword". You have kept every one.

choices.text: Send a poem back

ok.log: Your poem is worse than {npc}'s. {npc} treasures it above anything. The cranes fly both ways now.

fail.log: Your poem is so bad {npc} writes back only to correct it. A correspondence begins.

choices.text: Send a sword instead

effects.log: {npc} replies with a poem about the sword. It rhymes "sword" with "sword". You laugh for an hour.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stop, kindly

effects.log: The cranes stop. You miss them more than you expected.

events.text: The matchmaker returns from the great house with a formal refusal. The family found your prospects "thin" and your sword "loud". The matchmaker is apologetic, and also has three other houses lined up, one of which is reportedly very fond of loud swords.

choices.text: Laugh it off and see the next house

effects.log: The next house likes loud swords very much. You do not marry into it, but you make three good friends.

choices.text: Train until your prospects are thick

effects.log: A season of hard training. Your sword gets louder. You decide this is a personal triumph.

choices.text: Write the great house a gracious reply

effects.log: Your reply is so gracious the family regrets its refusal. They tell everyone. It does you no harm.

variants: A formal refusal from the great house, carried back by an apologetic matchmaker: your prospects are "thin", your sword "loud". The matchmaker has three more houses ready, and one of them is said to like a loud sword.

events.text: A matchmaker, grey-haired and sharp-eyed, has come to the door for your grown child. She sits down in your best chair, sets out a worn portfolio, and says: "Your child is much easier to sell than most."

choices.text: Let the child choose for themselves

effects.log: The matchmaker sighs at the new fashion. Your child chooses someone nobody expected, and is happy.

choices.text: Look through the portfolio together

effects.log: You and the matchmaker go through the candidates like old generals planning a campaign. Your child hides.

choices.text: Pay her well for her trouble (10 taels)

effects.log: She takes it, and tells you a secret about one of the great houses that she has kept for thirty years. (-10 taels)

events.text: For the first time in your life, a matchmaker comes to the door asking for you by name. You are no longer a child in anyone's eyes. The matchmaker measures you with an eye that has priced a thousand weddings and says: "Hm. We can work with this."

choices.text: Accept the matchmaker's services

effects.log: The matchmaker writes you up in a portfolio. Your description is generous. Your height has grown two fingers.

choices.text: Say you will find your own match

effects.log: The matchmaker laughs, not unkindly. "Everyone says that. I'll be back."

choices.text: Ask what the matchmaker charges

effects.log: The fee is outrageous and itemised. You learn more about marriage from the bill than from any book.

events.text: {npc} came into your house as the seal on an alliance. Now {his} birth family writes to {him} every month, and every letter asks, very gently, what your house intends: which sect you favour, where your silver goes, who visits. {npc} brings you the latest letter unopened.

choices.text: Read it together, openly

effects.log: Nothing in it is secret. Nothing in it is innocent. You draft a reply together that says nothing beautifully.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to answer as {he} likes

effects.log: {npc} goes very still. "You trust me with that?" You do. {He} writes back, and you never ask what.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stop writing home

effects.log: {npc} obeys. {He} also stops singing in the mornings. The house is quieter than it should be.

events.text: {npc}'s family and yours want opposite things at the provincial council: the same mine, the same river, the same seat. {npc}'s eldest sibling has come to stay, ostensibly to visit, and corners {npc} in the garden every evening. {npc} has started sleeping badly.

choices.text: Give up the mine for {npc}'s peace

mem.note: gave up the mine for me

effects.log: You yield the mine. The sibling goes home satisfied. {npc} sleeps through the night for the first time in a month. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Speak to the sibling yourself

ok.log: A long evening and a lot of wine. The sibling leaves with a compromise and a grudging respect.

fail.log: The conversation goes badly. The sibling leaves early and writes home about you in detail.

choices.text: Let {npc} decide which side to take

effects.log: {npc} takes neither side. {He} proposes a third way at the council, and both families grumble, and accept.

events.text: At a great banquet, {npc}'s family patriarch raises a cup and asks, in front of everyone, where {npc}'s loyalty lies now. The hall goes quiet. {npc} stands up slowly. Whatever {he} says next, one of the two houses will remember it for a generation.

choices.text: Stand up beside {npc} before {he} speaks

effects.log: {npc} says: "With both, as was agreed." You stand at {his} side. The patriarch drinks, and nods.

choices.text: Answer for {npc}

effects.log: You answer well. It does not matter. {npc} wanted to answer, and you took it from {him}.

choices.text: Trust {npc}, and stay seated

effects.log: {npc} speaks of two families and one table. The hall applauds. The patriarch looks proud and slightly beaten.

events.text: Namgung in-laws visit, and every Namgung visit includes a sword. They do not ask to spar. They simply mention, over dinner, that a certain sword form of yours has a weakness on the left, and wait. {npc} has quietly hidden the good teacups.

choices.text: Show them the left side

ok.log: There is no weakness on the left. The Namgung are delighted to have been wrong. They stay a week.

fail.log: There was a weakness on the left. The Namgung fix it for you, thoroughly. (-6 health)

choices.text: Talk poetry instead of swords

effects.log: The Namgung are confused. Then one of them recites a poem about a sword. It is a long dinner.

choices.text: Ask {npc} how to handle them

effects.log: "Praise the founder's calligraphy," {npc} murmurs. You do. The Namgung glow and forget the sword.

events.text: Dinner with the Tang in-laws. Every dish is exquisite, and the Tang are watching to see which dish you eat first. {npc} has warned you that the Tang never poison family, and has also warned you that the Tang have a very old joke about this exact moment.

choices.text: Eat the dish nearest to you, calmly

ok.log: The Tang matriarch laughs and pours you tea. You have passed a test you did not know the name of.

fail.log: A harmless spice that turns your tongue blue for a day. The Tang are delighted. The joke is very old. (-3 health)

choices.text: Ask the matriarch to choose for you

effects.log: The matriarch smiles slowly. "Clever." You are served from the matriarch's own plate. The Tang respect cleverness.

choices.text: Bring an antidote, openly, as a joke

effects.log: The Tang roar with laughter and examine your antidote critically. They give you a better one.

events.text: Your Jegal in-law has set up a game board in your study and invited you to play. Nobody says it is a test. Nobody needs to. The Jegal win battles before they are fought, and they judge their in-laws by how they lose. {npc} is watching from the door.

choices.text: Play your best and lose with grace

effects.log: You lose in forty moves. The Jegal nods. "Thirty would have been disappointing." A compliment, from a Jegal.

choices.text: Play strangely, against all theory

ok.log: Your strange move baffles the Jegal for an hour. You still lose, but the Jegal writes it down.

fail.log: You lose in twelve moves. The Jegal is very kind about it, which is worse.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to play in your place

effects.log: {npc} beats the in-law in fifty moves. The Jegal family has not been this surprised in a decade.

events.text: The Paeng in-laws have come from the north: six of them, loud, enormous, carrying sabres they will not put down. They are delighted with everything. They have broken two chairs and a gate post with sheer goodwill. {npc} looks embarrassed and very happy.

choices.text: Match them toast for toast

ok.log: You keep up until the last Paeng falls asleep at the table. You are a legend in the north by spring.

fail.log: You fall asleep first. The Paeng carry you to bed singing. They respect the attempt. (-5 health)

choices.text: Take them to train in the yard

effects.log: Sabre practice at dawn with six Paeng. You are bruised all over and they call you cousin.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to sing them the old songs

mem.note: let me sing for my family

effects.log: {npc} sings the northern songs. The huge Paeng weep openly. One of them blows a nose on a banner.

events.text: A rider comes in the night with your in-laws' great seal. Their house is at war with a rival family, and the alliance that brought {npc} into your house must be honoured now: swords, silver, or both. {npc} reads the letter twice and says nothing at all.

choices.text: Answer the call with your sword

effects.log: You ride before dawn. {npc} ties the cord of your sleeve with fingers that are not quite steady.

choices.text: Send silver instead of swords (30 taels)

effects.log: The silver goes. The in-laws accept it coolly. An alliance paid in coin is remembered as such. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Ride out to make peace between them

effects.log: You ride to the rival house under a white flag. Nobody has asked you to. Everyone is watching.

events.text: The battle line is a river ford. Your in-laws' banners on one bank, the rival family's on the other. Your in-laws' patriarch gives you the left flank, the worst place, to see what you will do with it. {npc}'s cousin fights at your side and does not trust you yet.

choices.text: Hold the left flank at any cost

ok.log: The left flank holds. The cousin pulls you out of the river by the collar and calls you family.

fail.log: The left flank bends but does not break. You are carried off it. (-14 health)

choices.text: Find a crossing upstream and turn them

ok.log: Your flanking crossing breaks the rival line without a long fight. Fewer dead on both banks.

fail.log: The upstream crossing is deeper than it looked. You arrive soaked and late. (-8 health)

choices.text: Shield the wounded at the ford

effects.log: You spend the battle dragging people out of the water, from both families. Nobody thanks you until later. (-5 health)

events.text: The war ends with a treaty, and you are named in it as a friend of your in-laws' house forever. When you come home, {npc} is waiting at the gate. {He} has heard every report from the ford, and has kept a lamp burning every night you were gone.

choices.text: Tell {npc} everything, every hour of it

effects.log: You talk until dawn. {npc} listens to all of it, and puts out the lamp at last.

choices.text: Say only that it is over

effects.log: {npc} does not ask. {He} takes your sword and hangs it up, and you both sleep.

choices.text: Bring {npc} the in-laws' gift of honour

effects.log: The gift is the family's old banner. {npc} hangs it beside yours. Two crests, one hall.

events.text: {npc} goes back to {his} family's great house each year at the new year rites. This year {he} asks you to come, which {he} has never done. The great house will be watching how you bow, where you sit and how you hold your cup.

choices.text: Go, and study their customs first

ok.log: You bow correctly to the correct people. The grandmother of the house nods once. {npc} is radiant.

fail.log: You bow to the wrong uncle. Everyone notices. Everyone is very kind about it. {npc} squeezes your hand.

choices.text: Go as you are, and be yourself

effects.log: The great house finds you unpolished and genuine. The children adore you. The elders reserve judgement.

choices.text: Send {npc} alone with fine gifts (15 taels)

effects.log: The gifts are admired. Your absence is also admired, in a different tone of voice. (-15 taels)

events.text: You host a feast for both families: yours and {npc}'s great house. Seating them is a campaign. Feeding them is a war. Keeping the two eldest uncles away from the subject of a duel fought forty years ago is a miracle you have not yet arranged.

choices.text: Seat the two uncles side by side

ok.log: The uncles glare, then start talking about the duel, then start laughing about it. A forty-year frost thaws.

fail.log: The uncles re-fight the duel with chopsticks. A dish is lost. The families agree it was entertaining. (-3 health)

choices.text: Seat them at opposite ends

effects.log: Distance works. The feast passes peacefully. The uncles shout at each other the length of the table, cheerfully.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to run the feast

effects.log: {npc} runs the feast like a general. Both families leave full, and slightly afraid of {him}.

events.text: It happens at breakfast: one spouse reaches for the last dumpling, another reaches for it too, and the table goes silent for far longer than a dumpling deserves. You realise your household has stopped being a family and started being a court, with factions.

choices.text: Cut the dumpling in exact halves

effects.log: Two exact halves. Everyone watches the knife. Peace for one breakfast; it is a beginning.

choices.text: Eat the dumpling yourself

effects.log: You eat it. Both spouses glare at you instead of each other. It is, in its way, a success.

choices.text: Order a hundred dumplings for tomorrow

effects.log: A hundred dumplings. Nobody can be jealous of a mountain. Everyone laughs, a little. (-5 taels)

events.text: You come home late from a long journey, expecting the usual chaos. Instead you find the whole household asleep in the main hall, together, around a brazier gone to embers: they waited up for you and fell asleep mid-story. Someone has saved you a bowl of soup.

choices.text: Sit down and eat the soup quietly

effects.log: Cold soup, a sleeping house, the embers ticking. You have never been richer.

choices.text: Cover each of them with a blanket

effects.log: One blanket each. In the morning nobody knows who did it, and everybody knows.

choices.text: Wake them all and tell the story

effects.log: Grumbling, then laughter, then a second pot of soup. Dawn finds the whole house awake and happy.

events.text: Three spouses, then more: your house is a great household now, and the district treats it like a small province. Merchants ask for appointments. The rice bill is the size of a sect's. A street child asks, in all seriousness, whether you are a king.

choices.text: Say yes, and give the child a coin

effects.log: The child tells everyone the king gave them a coin. Your household's reputation becomes legendary and slightly ridiculous.

choices.text: Hire a proper steward (20 taels)

effects.log: A steward with three abacuses and no sense of humour. The rice bill shrinks by a third. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Call the household together to give thanks

effects.log: A small rite in the ancestral hall, everyone in a line. It feels like the start of something old.

events.text: Your first night as emperor in the inner palace. A eunuch with a ledger explains the halls, the ranks, the seals, the order of precedence at every festival, and the hundred quarrels of a hundred years that you have just inherited. The ledger is very thick.

choices.text: Read the whole ledger tonight

effects.log: Dawn finds you on the last page. You know where every quarrel is buried, and who buried it.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to take charge of it

effects.log: {npc} takes the ledger and does not give it back for a decade. The inner palace has never run better.

choices.text: Abolish the order of precedence

ok.log: Astonishingly, it works. The inner palace sits where it likes at festivals, and grumbles happily.

fail.log: Chaos. Within a month the old order is quietly back, and the eunuch looks smug.

events.text: A famous painter has agreed to paint your household. The problem is the composition. Somebody must be in the centre, somebody must be on the left, and somebody, inevitably, must be partly behind a pine tree. The painter is waiting, brush wet.

choices.text: Put yourself behind the pine tree

effects.log: The portrait shows a household in perfect harmony and one ear behind a tree. It hangs in the hall for a hundred years.

choices.text: Arrange everyone by date of marriage

effects.log: Correct and fair, and everyone looks slightly stiff. The painter says it is very dignified.

choices.text: Have one portrait painted each (30 taels)

effects.log: One portrait each, the same size, hung in a row. Nobody can argue with a row. (-30 taels)

events.text: The household budget has become a battlefield. One courtyard has new silk curtains. Another has noticed. Petitions arrive on your desk, written very politely, each requesting curtains of equal or greater quality, with the receipts for the first curtains attached.

choices.text: Buy everyone the same curtains (20 taels)

effects.log: Identical curtains everywhere. The house looks like an inn. Peace, of a kind. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Give each courtyard a fixed allowance

effects.log: A fixed sum each, spent as they like. Someone buys a parrot. Nobody else is allowed to object.

choices.text: Take the first curtains down

effects.log: Down they come. Now everyone is equally unhappy, which is a sort of justice.

events.text: The alliance marriage is done. Your house and a great family are bound now: their name on your gate in small characters, yours on theirs. Their envoy hands you a token of the family, and a list of their enemies, which are now also yours. The list is long.

choices.text: Read the list of enemies carefully

effects.log: Three sects, two merchant houses, and one very old monk. You memorise every name.

choices.text: Ask for the list of friends too

effects.log: The envoy laughs and writes a second list. It is shorter. Great families make few friends.

choices.text: Hang the token over your gate

effects.log: Lesser houses bow lower at your gate now. A few old friends stop visiting. Every alliance has a price.

events.text: The matchmaker sent you to the Plum Teahouse. The matchmaker sent {npc} to the Plum Blossom Teahouse, across the canal. You both waited an hour, both left in a temper, and have now met by accident on the bridge between, each holding a matchmaker's note.

choices.text: Laugh, and find a third teahouse

effects.log: A third teahouse, no plums at all. You talk until they close. The matchmaker claims full credit.

choices.text: Complain together about the matchmaker

effects.log: Nothing unites two strangers like a shared grievance. You are friends by the bottom of the bridge.

choices.text: Apologise and part politely

effects.log: A polite bow on the bridge. Two days later {npc} sends a note: "Same bridge, tomorrow?"

events.text: The spring festival, and {npc} has found you in the crowd: the one the matchmaker introduced, who has become a friend in spite of the matchmaker. {He} has two tickets for the lantern boats and a look of great innocence that fools nobody.

choices.text: Take the lantern boat together

effects.log: The boat drifts among a thousand lanterns. You talk about nothing at all and remember all of it.

choices.text: Win {him} a prize at the archery stall

ok.log: A paper tiger, slightly crushed. {npc} carries it all night like a treasure.

mem.note: tried to win me a prize

fail.log: You miss every target. {npc} wins you a prize instead, and is unbearable about it.

choices.text: Say you are only friends

effects.log: "Of course," {npc} says, and takes the boat with someone else, and looks back once.

events.text: As part of the alliance, a young relative of {npc}'s great family comes to live in your house for a few years: to learn your ways, and, everyone understands, to keep the alliance honest. The fosterling is twelve, homesick, and has already set fire to a curtain.

choices.text: Train the fosterling with your own hand

mem.note: raised my kin as your own

effects.log: The fosterling becomes a fine young fighter and goes home speaking well of your house to everyone.

choices.text: Let {npc} raise the child

effects.log: {npc} is strict, warm and very good at it. The curtains survive. Mostly.

choices.text: Send the child home early, kindly

effects.log: The great family is cool about it. The child is delighted. You are unsure who won.

events.text: The first night after your first crime. You lie awake and listen to every footstep in the street. Every dog that barks is barking at you. In the morning the sun comes up as usual, the market opens, and nobody looks at you at all. Somehow that is worse.

choices.text: Swear it was the only time

effects.log: You swear it to the ceiling. The ceiling has heard such promises before.

choices.text: Count what you gained, coolly

effects.log: You count it twice. It is less than you thought. It is more than you had.

choices.text: Go to the temple and sit there all day

effects.log: An old monk sits beside you and says nothing for six hours. It helps more than you expected.

events.text: The fence works out of a pawnshop behind the fish market: {npc}, old, round, smiling, who smells of camphor and never asks where anything came from. {He} weighs your silver bracelet, looks at you over {his} spectacles, and offers a third of its worth.

choices.text: Take the third. Build a reputation

effects.log: {npc} smiles wider. "A reasonable young person. How rare." There will be better prices next time.

choices.text: Haggle hard

ok.log: Half its worth, after an hour. {npc} looks pained and pleased. "You'll do."

fail.log: {npc} lowers the offer for every minute you argue. You leave with less than the first offer.

choices.text: Take it elsewhere

effects.log: Elsewhere asks where it came from, and looks at your face for a long time. You go back to {npc}.

events.text: {npc} has a job for you, which {he} has never had before. A merchant's strongbox, a ledger inside it, and nothing else is to be taken. {He} will not say who wants the ledger. {He} says the merchant has cheated half the fish market.

choices.text: Take the job, take only the ledger

ok.log: In and out by the roof. Only the ledger. {npc} pays more than promised and asks no questions.

fail.log: A dog, a chase over three roofs, a torn sleeve. You get the ledger. You lose some skin. (-6 health)

choices.text: Read the ledger before you hand it over

effects.log: It records bribes paid to the harbour master. You hand it over. You remember every name.

choices.text: Refuse. You do not work blind

effects.log: {npc} shrugs. "Principles. Expensive things." {He} finds someone else.

events.text: The constables have raided the pawnshop. {npc} got out through the back with nothing but {his} spectacles and a list of every thief {he} ever bought from, your name among them. {He} is hiding in your woodshed and asks for one night.

choices.text: Hide {npc} for the night

effects.log: {npc} leaves before dawn for the south. In the woodshed {he} leaves the list, and a candle. You burn it.

choices.text: Ask for the list first

effects.log: {npc} hands it over without a word. You burn it. {He} goes at dawn, thinner in the face.

choices.text: Send {him} away at once

effects.log: {npc} goes. Three days later the constables know a great deal about your woodshed.

events.text: The Red Lantern Gang has claimed your streets. Their boss, {npc}, a lean figure with a scar through one eyebrow, has sent word: a tenth of everything, every month, or you work somewhere else. Nobody works anywhere else.

choices.text: Pay the tenth for now

effects.log: You pay. {npc} sends back a receipt, which is a strange courtesy for extortion. (-8 taels)

choices.text: Refuse, and see what happens

effects.log: Nothing happens for a week. Then your favourite rooftop is occupied by three very large people.

choices.text: Ask to meet {npc} face to face

effects.log: You meet in a noodle shop. {npc} is clever, tired and has thirty mouths to feed. That changes things.

events.text: The Red Lantern Gang and a bigger gang from the river are about to fight for the whole district. {npc} wants you on {his} side, on the rooftops, on the night. The river gang has sent you a message too, with a much larger number in it.

choices.text: Stand with {npc}

ok.log: The river gang breaks at the bridge. The Red Lanterns hold the district, and owe you.

fail.log: The rooftop fight goes badly. You hold anyway. The Red Lanterns carry you home. (-10 health)

choices.text: Take the river gang's silver

effects.log: The river gang wins. You are richer. {npc} knows exactly who opened the north gate.

choices.text: Broker a truce between them

ok.log: A truce at the temple, the streets divided by a canal. Nobody dies. Both gangs resent you a little.

fail.log: Both gangs think you are the other side's spy. You leave by the window. (-5 health)

events.text: {npc} is getting out. {He} has bought a small boat and wants to fish, like {his} father. {He} offers you the Red Lantern Gang: thirty people, the district, the receipts, and a lot of debts. "Or burn it all," {he} says. "Your choice. I'm done."

choices.text: Take over the gang

effects.log: Thirty people bow to you in a noodle shop. You are a boss now, which is mostly paperwork.

choices.text: Help the gang go honest

effects.log: A porter's guild, a night watch, a noodle shop. Half of them stay honest. It is more than half you expected.

choices.text: Let it scatter, and see {npc} off

effects.log: You stand on the dock as the boat goes. {npc} does not wave. {He} does look back.

events.text: The house was supposed to be empty. It is not. An old servant is asleep in the kitchen, and wakes as you pass, and stares at you over a bowl of cold rice. Neither of you moves. Somewhere upstairs, someone calls out to ask if everything is all right.

choices.text: Put a finger to your lips, and walk out

ok.log: The servant, slowly, puts a finger to their own lips. You leave empty-handed and unseen.

fail.log: The servant screams. You go out of the window with nothing and a description of your face behind you.

choices.text: Run, now

effects.log: Over the wall, through a vegetable patch, into the night. The house is lit behind you. (-3 health)

choices.text: Leave a coin on the table for the fright

effects.log: You put down a coin and go. The servant tells the story for years, and always mentions the coin.

events.text: Somebody else was robbed the same night, two streets over, and badly hurt. The constables have put the two jobs together. They are looking for one thief for both. The description they have is, unfortunately, quite a good one of you.

choices.text: Find the real culprit yourself

ok.log: A drunk with a cudgel and a pawn ticket. You leave the ticket where the constables will find it.

fail.log: The trail goes cold. The description stays warm. You stay indoors for a month.

choices.text: Leave the city for a season

effects.log: A season on a farm, in the hills. The description fades. You come back browner and slower.

choices.text: Change your face, your clothes, your walk

effects.log: A beard of soot, a limp, a merchant's hat. Your own landlord does not know you.

events.text: The old servant from that night finds you in the market. There is no mistaking it. They look at you for a long time, then say quietly: "My master would have hanged you. I didn't tell. My grandson is in prison for less."

choices.text: Ask about the grandson

effects.log: A stolen chicken, three years. You pay the fine. The servant does not thank you. They nod, once.

choices.text: Give the servant what you have

effects.log: The servant takes it, tucks it away, and walks off without a word. It is the right price. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Thank them, and walk away

effects.log: You walk away. You think about the grandson more often than you would like.

events.text: A new constable has come to the district: {npc}, quiet, polite, with an inkstone always at {his} belt. {He} does not chase. {He} notices. {He} has noticed, for example, that you are always awake on the nights when something goes missing.

choices.text: Lie low until {he} loses interest

effects.log: You lie low for two months. {npc} does not lose interest. {He} simply writes down that you lay low.

choices.text: Befriend {npc} openly

effects.log: Tea with the constable. {npc} is witty and kind and writes down everything you say.

choices.text: Plant a false trail for {him}

ok.log: {npc} follows the false trail to the next district. {He} will be back, and less polite.

fail.log: {npc} returns your false trail to you, neatly folded, with a note: "Nice try."

events.text: {npc} invites you to a game of stones at a teahouse. Between moves, {he} describes, very accurately, three of your jobs. {He} does not say they are yours. {He} only says it is a pity a person so careful works on the wrong side of the law.

choices.text: Keep playing, and win

ok.log: You win the game. {npc} laughs. "Well played." It is not clear which game {he} means.

fail.log: You lose, badly, distracted. {npc} gathers the stones. "Same time next week?"

choices.text: Ask what {he} wants

effects.log: {npc} wants a bigger thief: the magistrate's own clerk, who sells pardons. {He} thinks you could help.

choices.text: Leave the game unfinished

effects.log: {npc} finishes it alone, moving both colours, and notes the result in {his} book.

events.text: {npc} has you cornered at last: a dead-end alley, a warrant in {his} hand, the night watch at the alley mouth. {He} does not draw. {He} holds up the warrant and says, "There is another way this can end. But you'll have to choose it."

choices.text: Agree to help {him} catch the clerk

effects.log: A month later the pardon-selling clerk is in chains, and your warrant is lost in the river.

choices.text: Go over the wall

ok.log: Up and over, gone. {npc} does not chase. You hear {him} laugh, softly, behind you.

fail.log: The wall is too high. {npc} catches your ankle, gently, and that is that.

choices.text: Surrender to {npc}

effects.log: {npc} arrests you with great courtesy and speaks for you at the trial. One year, not ten.

events.text: The richest salt merchant in the province is building a vault under his warehouse, and boasting about it. A locksmith who worked on it, now unpaid and furious, comes to you with a plan of the vault drawn on a handkerchief, and a list of people you will need.

choices.text: Plan it carefully, for a year

effects.log: A year of watching, counting guards, learning the salt trade. You know the warehouse better than its owner.

choices.text: Ask who the merchant cheated

effects.log: Salt boilers paid in bad coin, a village's well bought and fenced. The locksmith has a long list.

choices.text: Burn the handkerchief and walk away

effects.log: The handkerchief burns. The locksmith goes to someone else. You read about the vault anyway, later.

events.text: You need a crew. The locksmith, of course. A cook who works in the merchant's house and hates the merchant. An acrobat from a travelling troupe who can fit through anything. The acrobat wants a bigger share. The cook wants no share at all, only revenge.

choices.text: Equal shares for everyone

effects.log: Equal shares. The acrobat grumbles and agrees. The cook says to give theirs to the salt boilers.

choices.text: Pay the acrobat more

effects.log: The acrobat is happy. Happy acrobats fit through smaller holes. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Do it with only the locksmith

effects.log: A small crew, a bigger risk, fewer tongues to wag afterwards.

events.text: The night of the job. Rain, as hoped. The cook has drugged the guards' soup with nothing worse than poppy tea. The acrobat is through the vent. The locksmith is at the inner door when you hear it: footsteps on the stairs, and a lantern.

choices.text: Hold the stairs yourself

ok.log: A guard, then two. You put them down quietly. The inner door opens behind you with a click.

fail.log: A hard fight in a narrow stair. You hold, barely. The inner door opens. (-10 health)

choices.text: Hide everyone and wait it out

ok.log: The lantern passes. It was the merchant, sleepless, counting coins in the dark. He goes back to bed.

fail.log: The lantern stops. A chase through the warehouse. You lose the acrobat's hat and nearly the acrobat. (-5 health)

choices.text: Abort the job. Out, now

effects.log: Out through the vent, into the rain. Nothing taken. Everyone alive. The locksmith weeps with rage.

events.text: Morning. The salt merchant's vault is empty, and the whole province is laughing. Your crew sits in a hut in the hills with more silver than any of you have ever seen. On the table is the merchant's other ledger: every bad coin paid to the salt boilers.

choices.text: Give the salt boilers their wages back

effects.log: Every boiler finds silver at the door one morning. The province calls the thief a hero. You keep a fifth.

choices.text: Split it all, and scatter

effects.log: The crew scatters to four provinces. You never see them again. The silver lasts a long time.

choices.text: Send the ledger to the governor
