effects.log: The merchant is ruined by his own ledger. The governor never asks who sent it.

events.text: The purse you lifted at the market is very light. Inside, three coppers, a pawn ticket for a wedding ring, and a letter from a doctor about a sick child. You look back at the crowd and see the owner, a worn-out porter, searching the ground with both hands.

choices.text: Put it back in the porter's path

effects.log: The porter finds it on the ground and weeps with relief. You walk away with nothing and a lighter chest.

choices.text: Put it back with silver added

effects.log: The porter finds the purse heavier than it was. They look around, frightened and grateful. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Keep it. A job is a job

effects.log: Three coppers. You spend them on a bun you cannot taste.

events.text: You have broken into what you thought was a rich merchant's storehouse. It is a widow's home. The silver on the shelf is a funeral fund, wrapped in paper and labelled in a shaky hand: for the burial, do not touch.

choices.text: Leave everything, and mend the lock

effects.log: You fix the lock better than it was. The widow tells the street a spirit has blessed her door.

choices.text: Take it. She will not need it yet

effects.log: You take it. For weeks you cannot pass that street. Some coins are heavier than they weigh.

choices.text: Leave some silver of your own

effects.log: You add five coins to the paper. The burial fund, you think, should be generous. (-5 taels)

events.text: A street child has been following you for three days. Today they finally speak up: they saw you on the roofs, and they want to learn. They are hungry and fast and very sure of themselves. They are about the age you were when you first went hungry.
events.arc: The Child Who Wants to Learn

choices.text: Teach them a trade instead

effects.log: You find them a place with a carpenter. They sulk for a month and then become very good at joints.

choices.text: Teach them the rooftops

effects.log: The child is a natural. In a year, they are faster than you. You are not sure how you feel about it.

choices.text: Feed them, and send them home

effects.log: A bowl of noodles and a coin. They go, and come back the next day. And the next. (-3 taels)

events.text: An old thief at the night market, the kind with no fingers to spare, tells you the code: never steal from a temple, never from a wedding, never from someone who has less than you. Break it, and the others will stop warning you when the constables come.

choices.text: Swear by the code

effects.log: The old thief nods. From now on, strangers on the roofs whistle a warning when the watch passes.

choices.text: Ask who made the rules

effects.log: "Thieves who got old," the old thief says. "The ones who didn't follow it, didn't."

choices.text: Say the code is for the weak

effects.log: The old thief shrugs and turns away. Nobody on the roofs knows your name any more.

events.text: A shout from the street, a whistle, and the night watch is after you. Across the rooftops of the old quarter, tiles slipping, laundry poles in the way, a cat that refuses to move. The watch has a new member who is fast. Very fast.

choices.text: Outrun them across the roofs

ok.log: You leap the canal roof and they do not. A cheer from below: a few people are watching, and they like you.

fail.log: A tile slips, you drop into a courtyard full of washing. You escape wrapped in someone's sheet. (-6 health)

choices.text: Drop into a crowded festival street

effects.log: You drop into a lantern parade and become one more dancer. The watch searches a hundred dancers in vain.

choices.text: Stop, and wait for the fast one

effects.log: The fast one arrives breathless. You bow. They bow back, confused. You run again while they are still bowing.

events.text: A job has left you with a cut you cannot take to any honest doctor. There is one in the alleys behind the dye works who asks no questions, charges double, and keeps a cage of finches that sing while she stitches.

choices.text: Pay the alley doctor (12 taels)

effects.log: Neat stitches, a finch's song, and no questions. You leave lighter in the purse and the body. (-12 taels)

choices.text: Stitch it yourself

ok.log: Your stitches are ugly and they hold. You learn more about wounds than you wanted.

fail.log: The cut goes bad. A week of fever. You see the alley doctor anyway. (-8 health)

choices.text: Go to the temple physicians

effects.log: The monk looks at the cut, looks at you, and says nothing. A gift you cannot repay.

events.text: Your sect brothers and sisters praise you at dinner for your honest heart. You have stolen four times this season. An elder looks at you a moment too long. Righteous sects do not keep thieves; they keep a punishment for them that is spoken of only in whispers.

choices.text: Confess to the elder

effects.log: A long silence. A severe penance. Then the elder says, "Few would have confessed." You are not expelled.

choices.text: Stop stealing, and say nothing

effects.log: You stop. The elder stops looking. Your secret becomes a stone you carry, and learn to carry.

choices.text: Steal only from the corrupt from now on

effects.log: A righteous thief, then. The elder would not approve. You suspect the founder might.

events.text: The Cult has heard about your quick hands. An elder of the mountain sends you a single order: steal the membership rolls of a righteous sect's hidden branch. The order does not say what happens to the people on the rolls. It does not need to.

choices.text: Steal the rolls and deliver them

ok.log: The rolls reach the mountain. You are favoured. You try not to think about what happens next.

fail.log: Guards. A hard escape. The elder is displeased, coldly. (-10 health)

choices.text: Steal them, and burn them

effects.log: You report the rolls lost in a fire, which is true. The elder looks at you a long time. You live.

choices.text: Refuse the task

effects.log: Refusing the Cult is a quiet thing that becomes very loud. You start sleeping with a knife.

events.text: Your faction's stronghold expects a share of every job done in its territory. The quartermaster, a pleasant scarred person with an abacus, has a list of your recent work. It is complete. It is correct. The share is a third.
events.arc: The Black Path Takes Its Cut

choices.text: Pay the third

effects.log: The quartermaster beams. Your name goes up on the stronghold board, and the stronghold watches your back. (-15 taels)

choices.text: Argue the list is inflated

ok.log: The quartermaster laughs and settles for a tenth. "For courage," they say.

fail.log: The quartermaster adds a fee for wasting their time. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Offer a job instead of silver

effects.log: The stronghold has a job. It is a hard one. You come back with the silver and a bruise.

events.text: An old beggar sits on your doorstep, eating your persimmons. "The Beggars' Sect sees everything," the beggar says, not unkindly. "We saw you on the merchant's roof. We will not tell. We would like, in return, a favour."

choices.text: Ask what the favour is

effects.log: A dozen sacks of rice from a hoarder's granary, delivered to the bridge where the beggars sleep.

choices.text: Give the beggar silver now (8 taels)

effects.log: The beggar takes it and nods. The Beggars' Sect will not tell. They will remember you paid quickly. (-8 taels)

choices.text: Feed the beggar dinner first

effects.log: Over dinner the beggar tells you who in town actually deserves robbing. It is a long list. It is very useful.

events.text: Your knees ache on the rooftops now. Last week you misjudged a jump you used to make asleep. You still have your rope, your picks, your soft shoes, and a little silver put aside. A thief who stays too long ends one way.

choices.text: Retire, and open a small shop

effects.log: A locksmith's shop. Your locks are the best in the city. Your old friends find them very frustrating.

choices.text: One last job, then retire

ok.log: The last job goes smoothly. You hang up the rope with a heavy purse. Everyone says one last job. You meant it.

fail.log: The last job goes wrong, as last jobs do. You get out, just. You hang up the rope anyway. (-8 health)

choices.text: Keep going. You are not done

effects.log: You stretch your knees every morning now. You are slower and cleverer. It evens out, mostly.

events.text: The silver you took from the tax office has tiny marks punched into every coin: a lotus, invisible unless you know where to look. Every money changer in the province has been told to look. You have a sack of very beautiful, very useless coins.

choices.text: Melt it down

ok.log: A borrowed forge, a long night, a few ingots with no lotus at all.

fail.log: Burnt fingers and a lump of silver that looks suspicious. You sell it for a fraction. (-4 health)

choices.text: Return it, anonymously

effects.log: The silver appears on the tax office steps one morning. The magistrate is baffled and a little afraid.

choices.text: Give it to the beggars at the bridge

effects.log: The beggars cannot spend it either, but they use it to bribe a magistrate who never looks at coins. Everyone is happy.

events.text: Your face is on the town gate. Not a good likeness, but not bad enough, and the reward under it is insultingly small. A child is studying it carefully, then studying you, then the poster again, with a frown of deep concentration.

choices.text: Wink at the child and walk on

ok.log: The child winks back, delighted to share a secret, and says nothing to anyone.

fail.log: The child shouts "It's you!" You leave town at a run, followed by a growing crowd.

choices.text: Tear the poster down at night

effects.log: One less poster. In the morning, two new ones. The reward has gone up. You feel oddly flattered.

choices.text: Complain to a constable about the reward

effects.log: The constable agrees the reward is too small. Neither of you mentions whose face it is.

events.text: A constable stops you at the bridge. {npc} looks at your face, at the poster in {his} hand, and back at your face. Then {he} looks at the river for a while. "It is a very expensive river," {he} says, to nobody.

choices.text: Pay for the river (20 taels)

effects.log: Silver changes hands. {npc} studies the river with great interest until you are gone. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Talk your way past

ok.log: A long story about a twin, very convincing. {npc} does not believe a word, but enjoys it, and lets you go.

fail.log: The twin story does not work. The river was cheaper. You spend a year thinking about that.

choices.text: Jump into the river

effects.log: Cold water, a long swim, a ruined pair of shoes. {npc} is still laughing on the bridge. (-4 health)

events.text: {npc} knows. {He} knew before the posters went up, and {he} has said nothing. But {npc}'s family is poor, and the reward on your head went up again this week. {He} has started to look at you as if {he} were counting something.

choices.text: Talk to {npc} honestly about it

effects.log: {npc} is ashamed you noticed. "I would never," {he} says. You both hear how tired {he} sounds.

choices.text: Give {npc}'s family money (20 taels)

effects.log: The silver goes to {npc}'s family. {npc} cannot decide whether it is kindness or a purchase. (-20 taels)

choices.text: Stop seeing {npc}

effects.log: You stop visiting. {npc} notices. People who feel distrusted begin to wonder why they bother being trusted.

events.text: A constable visits {npc}'s home and leaves after an hour. You see it from a rooftop. Tonight, {npc} knocks on your door, alone, and asks to come in. {His} hands are empty. {His} face is very pale.

choices.text: Let {npc} in and listen

effects.log: "They asked. I said nothing," {npc} says. "But next time, I don't know." You leave the city at dawn.

choices.text: Leave by the back window

effects.log: You leave by the window. You never learn why {npc} came. Some doors stay shut.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to come with you

effects.log: {npc} cannot leave {his} family. {He} cries, and refuses, and gives you {his} travel cloak.

events.text: Constables at dawn, a warrant, and a search of every lodging in the street. Yours is fourth. Under the floor is everything: the picks, the rope, a few things that are recognisably not yours. You have the time it takes to search three rooms.

choices.text: Move it all to the neighbour's roof

ok.log: Up, over, down, in place before the constables reach your door. The neighbour's pigeons are confused.

fail.log: A tile slips, a bundle falls into the street. The constables are very pleased.

choices.text: Leave it and look innocent

ok.log: The constable knocks on the floor twice and moves on. Your heart starts again.

fail.log: The constable knocks on the floor twice and stops. Picks, rope, and two years.

choices.text: Burn it all in the stove now

effects.log: Everything burns. The constables find a lot of smoke and an honest-looking person. (-10 taels)

events.text: Somebody is talking. Three of your hiding places have been raided in a month. The night market says the informant is a noodle seller, or a monk, or a one-eyed porter, depending on who you ask. Somebody knows a great deal about you.

choices.text: Set three traps, three false stories

ok.log: Only one story reaches the constables: the one you told the noodle seller. You move on, quietly.

fail.log: All three stories reach the constables. Everyone is talking. You leave the district.

choices.text: Move to another city

effects.log: A new city, new rooftops. The informant's knowledge is suddenly worth very little.

choices.text: Find the informant and pay them more

effects.log: The noodle seller. Now the noodle seller informs on the constables instead. (-15 taels)

events.text: The road out of the city has a new checkpoint. Every traveller's face is checked against a stack of posters. The line moves slowly. Ahead of you, a wedding procession, a merchant with three carts of cabbage, and a monk who keeps looking back at you.

choices.text: Join the wedding procession

ok.log: You carry a lantern and sing very loudly. Nobody checks the face of anyone in a wedding.

fail.log: The bride's mother has never seen you before and says so, loudly. You run.

choices.text: Hide among the cabbages (5 taels)

effects.log: The merchant charges for the privilege. You arrive in the next city smelling of cabbage. (-5 taels)

choices.text: Ask the monk why they keep looking

effects.log: The monk is also wanted, for stealing temple bread for orphans. You go round the checkpoint together through the fields.

events.text: You notice it all at once: the watch doubled on your street, a constable outside your teahouse, your name said quietly by strangers. The authorities are close now. For the first time, being a thief feels less like a trade and more like being hunted.

choices.text: Go to ground for a while

effects.log: You live like a monk for a season. It is very boring. It is also how old thieves get old.

choices.text: Lay a false trail to the next province

effects.log: A pawned ring there, a sighting there. The constables ride east. You stay exactly where you are.

choices.text: Enjoy it. You are famous

effects.log: You stroll through the market in broad daylight. Reckless. Glorious. Probably a mistake.

events.text: You are a footpad: the lowest rank of the trade, and you know it. Real thieves look through you at the night market. Tonight a drunken official staggers home alone along the canal, purse swinging, singing a song about his own honesty.

choices.text: Lift the purse and vanish

ok.log: The purse is fat with bribes. The official keeps singing about honesty all the way home.

fail.log: The official is less drunk than he looked, and punches very hard. (-4 health)

choices.text: See him home safely instead

effects.log: You walk him home. At his door he gives you a coin and calls you an honest citizen. You keep a straight face.

choices.text: Follow him to learn where he lives

effects.log: A big house, a weak lock, a dog that is all bark. You file it away for when you are more than a footpad.

events.text: The thieves of the night market finally notice you. A sharp-eyed elder of the trade sets you a test: lift a specific jade token from a specific merchant's belt, in daylight, at the busiest hour, and bring it back before the noon bell.

choices.text: Take the test

ok.log: Noon bell, and the token is on the elder's table. Thieves look at you differently now.

fail.log: The merchant catches your wrist. You twist free and run. The elder sighs. "Again, next month." (-3 health)

choices.text: Ask what the token is for

effects.log: It is a pass to the merchant's own vault. The test was a job all along. You are learning.

choices.text: Decline. You work alone

effects.log: The elder shrugs. Alone, then. The night market will not warn you about the watch.

events.text: You are a Thief now, not a footpad: the night market makes room at the good tables, and the fences quote better prices. With rank comes a request: a guild wants a sealed letter out of a magistrate's study before the court sits tomorrow.

choices.text: Take the commission

ok.log: The letter is out by midnight, the seal unbroken. The guild pays and asks your name.

fail.log: The magistrate's study has a second lock nobody mentioned. You get half the job done. (-6 health)

choices.text: Read the letter first

effects.log: It names the guild's own bribes. You deliver it, and keep a copy, in case.

choices.text: Refuse. Courts are trouble

effects.log: You turn it down. Two days later the thief who took it is in prison. Courts are trouble.

events.text: The thieves' guild of the provincial capital invites you to join: protection, lawyers, safe houses, and a tenth of everything. The guildmaster is a smiling grandmother who knits through the whole meeting and never once looks at the knitting.

choices.text: Join the guild

effects.log: You are given a knitted scarf, a password and a safe house. The grandmother pats your hand. (-5 taels)

choices.text: Ask what happens to those who leave

effects.log: The grandmother smiles. "Nobody leaves, dear. They retire." The knitting needles click.

choices.text: Decline, very politely

effects.log: The grandmother nods and keeps knitting. Somehow the declining feels like the riskier choice.

events.text: They call you the Phantom Thief now. Songs are sung about you in the teahouses, mostly wrong. Children play at being you with paper masks. A constable you have never met has sworn an oath at the ancestral shrine to catch you before {his} hair turns grey.

choices.text: Leave the constable a respectful note

effects.log: Your note praises {npc}'s dedication. {npc} frames it, and doubles the night watch.

choices.text: Stop, while you are a legend

effects.log: Silence for a year. The legend grows larger in the silence. The constable does not believe you have stopped.

choices.text: Plan a theft worthy of the songs

effects.log: The Governor's jade seal. Impossible. Which is exactly the point.

events.text: You send a card, as the songs say you do: "At the hour of the rat, I will take the Governor's jade seal." The Governor's residence is ringed by two hundred guards, and {npc} stands at its gate personally, with a lantern and a very determined face.

choices.text: Go in through the front gate

ok.log: Disguised as a guard reporting to {npc}. {npc} sends you inside personally. The seal is gone by the hour of the rat.

fail.log: {npc} looks at your disguise a long moment and says, "No." The songs get a new, sadder verse.

choices.text: Go over the roof

ok.log: Over the roof, through the skylight, out the drain. The seal is gone. The city sings for a month.

fail.log: A roof tile, a fall, a narrow escape without the seal. The songs call it a draw. (-10 health)

choices.text: Take nothing, and leave the seal moved

effects.log: At dawn the seal is found in the Governor's teacup. Nothing taken. The Governor never sleeps well again.

events.text: Years of the chase. {npc}'s hair is grey now. One night {he} finds you on a rooftop, alone, unarmed, and sits down a little distance away. "I am retiring," {he} says. "I would like to know your face, once. I will tell nobody."

choices.text: Take off the mask

effects.log: {npc} looks for a long time, and laughs. "You bought me a bun once, in the market." {He} keeps the secret.

choices.text: Keep the mask on

effects.log: {npc} nods. "Fair." The two of you watch the sun come up over the roofs, enemies and something else.

choices.text: Give {him} the jade seal to return

effects.log: {npc} returns the seal and retires a hero. The songs say the Phantom Thief let the old constable win.

events.text: Someone has been leaving your calling card at robberies you did not commit. Poor houses, a temple, a widow's shop. The songs in the teahouses are turning ugly. A Phantom Thief who robs the poor is no legend at all.

choices.text: Hunt the imposter down

ok.log: A failed footpad with a printing block. You leave the imposter tied up at the magistrate's gate with every stolen thing.

fail.log: The imposter is clever. The robberies stop, but the ugly songs do not.

choices.text: Repay every victim yourself

effects.log: Each victim finds the stolen value returned with your card. The songs change back. (-25 taels)

choices.text: Let the legend take the stain

effects.log: You do nothing. The legend darkens. Children stop playing at being you.

events.text: A young thief has started calling themselves the Second Phantom. They are very fast and very bad at the parts that are not running. Tonight they have been cornered in a warehouse by thirty constables, and the whole quarter is watching.

choices.text: Get them out

ok.log: A smoke pot, a rope, two Phantoms gone over the roofs. The quarter cheers. You give the youngster a long lecture.

fail.log: You get them out, and leave some skin on the warehouse roof. (-8 health)

choices.text: Let them learn the hard way

effects.log: The Second Phantom spends a year in prison. When they come out, they come to find you, humbler.

choices.text: Send the constables a false sighting

effects.log: Half the constables run to the river after a Phantom who is not there. The youngster slips away.

events.text: A blind singer in the market sings the ballad of the Phantom Thief. In this version you are three times taller, you fly, and you once stole the moon to give it to a poor village. The crowd gives coins. The blind singer is doing very well out of you.

choices.text: Give the singer a coin and listen

effects.log: The singer bows towards you exactly, though blind. "Thank you, Phantom," they murmur. You leave very fast.

choices.text: Correct one detail

effects.log: You mention you have never stolen the moon. The crowd boos you. The singer adds a verse about doubters.

choices.text: Commission a new verse (10 taels)

effects.log: The new verse is about the Phantom feeding orphans. It becomes the most popular one. (-10 taels)

events.text: For the first time, the underworld's own unwritten list of great thieves has your name at the top: the Phantom Thief, who takes what cannot be taken. Thieves of three provinces raise their cups to you tonight, and none of them knows your face.

choices.text: Raise your own cup, anonymously

effects.log: You drink to yourself in a crowded teahouse among thieves who would give an arm to meet you.

choices.text: Take the next job to deserve it

effects.log: Legends need feeding. You start planning something that will be sung about for a hundred years.

choices.text: Feel only the weight of it

effects.log: A name at the top is a target. You light a candle at the temple, for luck, and for the ones you took from.

events.text: Famine in the county, and the magistrate's granary is full. He is selling rice at ten times its price to the people he is supposed to feed. The granary is guarded by four men who are as hungry as everyone else, and who hate the magistrate too.

choices.text: Talk to the guards

ok.log: The guards agree to be looking the other way on the night of the new moon, for a sack each.

fail.log: One guard is loyal, or afraid. The others shake their heads. It will have to be quiet.

choices.text: Find the magistrate's private ledger first

effects.log: Every bag of rice sold, every bribe received. The ledger is a weapon. The granary is a mission.

choices.text: Leave it. Too many eyes

effects.log: You leave the county. On the road out, you pass the hungry villages, and do not look.

events.text: The night of the new moon. The granary doors are open. Carts from four villages wait at the edge of the fields, the farmers' faces pale in the dark. You have until the first cock-crow to move a whole granary's worth of rice to people who need it.

choices.text: Organise the carts like an army

ok.log: Every sack moved by cock-crow. Four villages eat. The magistrate wakes to an empty granary and a full county.

fail.log: Most of the rice gets out. The last cart is caught at dawn. The farmers scatter, and you take the blame. (-6 health)

choices.text: Take rice for the villages, and silver for you

effects.log: The villages eat. You eat better. Nobody among the farmers begrudges it, much.

choices.text: Send the ledger to the Censorate too

effects.log: The rice goes to the villages; the ledger goes to the capital. The magistrate is gone by spring.

events.text: The tax collector of the river county collects twice: once for the throne, once for himself. He travels with a strongbox and two bodyguards, and stops every night at the same inn, where he drinks and sleeps very soundly on the box.

choices.text: Steal the strongbox from under him

ok.log: You replace the box with a box of river stones. You return the second tax to the villages, mostly.

fail.log: He wakes up, the bodyguards wake up, the inn wakes up. You leave by the roof empty-handed. (-6 health)

choices.text: Send his double ledger to the governor

effects.log: The governor reads it with interest. The tax collector's travelling days are over.

choices.text: Leave him a frightening note

effects.log: "I know about the second tax." The collector collects only once that year, and sleeps badly.

events.text: Fever in the city, and the only apothecary with willow bark has tripled the price and locked the rest in the cellar. The poor quarter is dying for want of it. The apothecary's cellar lock is old. You could open it in your sleep.

choices.text: Empty the cellar to the poor quarter

ok.log: By morning the poor quarter's clinics have more willow bark than the apothecary. The fever breaks.

fail.log: You get half of it out before the watch comes. Half is a great deal. (-5 health)

choices.text: Take it, and sell it at a fair price

effects.log: A fair price, at a back door. The quarter calls you the honest apothecary. The irony is not lost on you.

choices.text: Shame the apothecary publicly instead

effects.log: A placard on his door. A crowd. By noon the price is fair again. By evening he has closed the shop.

events.text: Your cellmate is an old forger with a remarkable memory for the prison's plans, which they drew for a bribe thirty years ago, before they were caught for something else. They will share the plans, they say, for a place on the way out.

choices.text: Agree. Two go together

effects.log: The forger draws the plans in rice paste on the cell wall, then eats them. The drains, the laundry, the bell tower.

choices.text: Ask for the plans, then go alone

effects.log: The forger looks at you for a long time. "So that's who you are." The plans come anyway, incomplete.

choices.text: Refuse. Serve your time

effects.log: You sit, breathe and wait. The forger shrugs and finds another partner.

events.text: Weeks of work. A loose stone behind the latrine, a sliver of iron filed into a key, a guard who drinks on the night of the full moon. Tonight it is the full moon. The stone moves. The drain beyond it is narrow, and very, very dark.

choices.text: Go through the drain

ok.log: An hour in the dark and the filth, then the river and the stars. You are out, and wanted.

fail.log: The drain narrows to nothing. You come back through the latrine to a very angry guard. Three more years. (-8 health)

choices.text: Bribe the drunk guard instead (30 taels)

effects.log: The guard takes the silver and falls asleep with the gate open. You walk out like a visitor. (-30 taels)

choices.text: Put the stone back. Not tonight

effects.log: You put the stone back. Something felt wrong. The next morning they search every cell.

events.text: One of the guards owes money to a gang outside, and the gang has started threatening the guard's family. You know the gang. You know the boss's habits. The guard knows you know, and has started bringing extra rice to your cell.

choices.text: Write the gang a letter for the guard

effects.log: Your letter persuades the gang. The guard's family is safe. The guard leaves your cell door unlocked at night.

choices.text: Ask the guard to let you go in return

ok.log: A door left open, a wagon of laundry. You are out. The guard's family is safe. Everyone keeps quiet.

fail.log: The guard panics and reports you. A beating, and a colder cell. (-5 health)

choices.text: Eat the rice and do nothing

effects.log: You eat well for a month. The guard stops bringing rice. Nothing else changes.

events.text: Your new cellmate is a farmer accused of stealing a magistrate's horse. You know who really stole the magistrate's horse. It was you, three years ago, and the horse is happily pulling a plough two counties away.

choices.text: Confess, and free the farmer

effects.log: The farmer goes home. Two more years for you. The farmer's family sends you rice cakes every new year.

choices.text: Teach the farmer to survive in here

effects.log: You teach the farmer to fight, to bribe, to sleep with one eye open. It is the least you can do.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: You say nothing. The farmer talks about home every night. You learn the names of all their children.

events.text: The cell door shuts. It makes a sound you will hear in dreams for years. Your cellmates look you over without interest. Someone has scratched ten thousand marks into the wall by the window. Someone else has scratched a very good drawing of a peach.

choices.text: Add your own mark to the wall

effects.log: One mark. It looks very small next to ten thousand. You make a second one the next night.

choices.text: Ask who drew the peach

effects.log: An old prisoner smiles. "Me. Twenty years ago. I have never tasted a better one." You become friends.

choices.text: Start planning the way out

effects.log: You count the guards' footsteps until dawn. Every prison has a door. Some are just harder to see.

events.text: A country inn, a hot meal, a bed. The innkeeper keeps glancing at you over the counter, then at a paper on the wall behind, then at you. A rider with a constable's badge has just tied up a horse in the yard outside.

choices.text: Leave money and go out the back

effects.log: Out the back, through a cabbage field, into the woods. The meal was very good. (-3 taels)

choices.text: Sit tight and eat slowly

ok.log: The constable orders soup, eats it, and leaves. The innkeeper says nothing. You tip generously.

fail.log: The constable recognises you. A fight in the yard, a stolen horse, a long night ride. (-5 health)

events.text: The only way out of the province is the ferry, and the ferry has a constable on it who checks every face. The ferryman, an old woman with arms like ropes, has seen your poster. She has also seen the constable. She looks at both of you and spits in the river.

choices.text: Pay the ferryman to hide you (10 taels)

effects.log: Under a tarpaulin with the ducks. She curses the ducks loudly whenever the constable comes near. (-10 taels)

choices.text: Help her pole the ferry, as crew

effects.log: You pole the whole crossing with your face to the water. The constable never looks at the crew.

choices.text: Swim the river at night

effects.log: Cold, dark, a long current. You crawl out a mile downstream, alive. (-6 health)

events.text: A mountain village where nobody asks your name. They need someone to mend a roof, someone to dig a well, someone to frighten off a bandit band that comes every autumn. They offer a hut and rice. They do not look at posters.

choices.text: Stay the winter and work

effects.log: A roof, a well, and a bandit band that leaves very quickly. The village gives you a name of their own.

choices.text: Stay only till the bandits come

ok.log: The bandits come. They go. The village feasts you, and you leave in the morning before the thanks get dangerous.

fail.log: The bandits are tougher than the village thought. You win, barely. (-10 health)

choices.text: Rest one night and move on

effects.log: One night's sleep under a roof. You leave a coin on the mat and go on before dawn.

events.text: A bounty hunter has been on your trail for a month: patient, polite, leaving notes at every inn you leave. Tonight the note is under your own door. "I am tired, and so are you. Tea at the shrine at dawn. No weapons."

choices.text: Go to the shrine

ok.log: Tea. A long talk. The hunter agrees to report you dead in a river. You pay for the tea.

fail.log: The hunter meant it about the weapons. Their friends did not. You run again. (-8 health)

choices.text: Leave before dawn

effects.log: You leave. At the next inn, another note: "Rude." The chase goes on.

choices.text: Set a trap at the shrine

effects.log: The hunter walks around your trap, sits down, and pours two cups of tea. "Really?"

events.text: You have become a wandering herbalist, a monk, a salt peddler, and once, for a terrible week, a travelling fortune-teller. Your current disguise is wearing thin. A village has asked the fortune-teller to predict the harvest.

choices.text: Predict a good harvest, confidently

ok.log: The harvest is excellent. The village begs you to stay. You leave at once, before next year.

fail.log: The harvest is poor. The village comes looking for the fortune-teller. The fortune-teller is a salt peddler now.

choices.text: Teach them to read the weather themselves

effects.log: Clouds, ants, the smell of the wind. The village never needs a fortune-teller again.

choices.text: Drop the disguise and be someone new

effects.log: A night in the woods, a change of clothes. In the morning, a wandering scholar walks out the other side.

events.text: You got away. The walls, or the rooftops, are behind you, the sky is enormous, and every road has a guardpost. You have nothing but the clothes you fled in and a name that is now worth silver to anyone who sees you. Freedom is terrifying.

choices.text: Head for the mountains

effects.log: Mountains do not read posters. You live on roots and snow-water and are very, very happy.

choices.text: Head for the biggest city

effects.log: A million faces. Yours is one more. In the crowd, you are invisible for the first time in years.

choices.text: Go home, just once, to see it

ok.log: You stand outside the old house at night. A lamp in the window. You go without knocking.

fail.log: The constables expected exactly that. You get away, barely. (-6 health)

events.text: You realise it at the night market: the thieves no longer look through you. They look at you. Someone has saved you a seat. A fence offers a price before you ask. Somewhere along the way, you stopped being a footpad and became a Thief.

choices.text: Sit in the saved seat

effects.log: The seat is warm and the tea is good. You listen more than you talk. That is how you will stay in it.

choices.text: Buy the whole table a round

effects.log: Generosity among thieves is remembered precisely. (-8 taels)

choices.text: Remember the footpad you were

effects.log: You buy a bun for the ragged footpad at the edge of the market. Nobody did that for you.

events.text: The richest house in town is holding a wedding. Every guest brings a gift, and the gift room is guarded by a single nephew who is already drunk. The thieves' code says never steal from a wedding. The silver says otherwise.

choices.text: Respect the code. Leave it

effects.log: You go to the wedding as a guest instead, eat well, and dance. The nephew is very happy to see you.

choices.text: Take one gift only

ok.log: One gift, nobody notices. The bride writes thank-you notes for it anyway.

fail.log: The nephew is not as drunk as he looked. A chase through the wedding. The bride is furious.

choices.text: Guard the gift room yourself

effects.log: Another thief tries for the gift room at midnight. You stop them. The family thinks you are a guest of great virtue.

events.text: The offering box at the mountain temple is heavy with pilgrims' coins. The monks are at evening prayers. Nobody is watching except a carved stone bodhisattva with a chipped nose and an expression of tremendous patience.

choices.text: Put a coin in instead

effects.log: You put in a coin and go. The bodhisattva's expression does not change. You feel it has noted the coin.

choices.text: Take from it

effects.log: Ten taels. On the way down the mountain you slip on every step. Coincidence, probably.

choices.text: Sit with the statue a while

effects.log: An hour of silence with the bodhisattva. When you leave, you have forgotten why you came.

events.text: The child of the constable who has hunted you for years gets lost in the night market, crying, alone. You are the only one who notices. The constable will be frantic. The constable is also, at this moment, three streets away searching for you.

choices.text: Bring the child to the constable

ok.log: The constable takes the child and looks at you a long time. That night, the hunt is called off for a week.

fail.log: The constable takes the child, thanks you, and arrests you. Gently. Very apologetically.

choices.text: Take the child to the night watch post

effects.log: You leave the child with the watch and slip away. The child describes you very accurately later.

choices.text: Pay a noodle seller to look after them

effects.log: The noodle seller feeds the child until the constable comes. The constable never learns who paid. (-3 taels)
